https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/14/m.summary_zh: 马金德证实他正积极参与有关可能组建反对派联盟的讨论，并表示，如果这样的安排能为击败执政党提供最大机会，他愿意与前副总统阿提库·阿布巴卡或尼日利亚民主大会党总统候选人彼得·奥比合作。当被直接问及是否愿意与其他主要反对派人物结盟时，马金德给予肯定答复。
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/14/m.body: *Says failure to honour unity govt deal severed relationship with Tinubu Oyo State Governor and presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Seyi Makinde, has said opposition parties must forge an alliance and rally behind the presidential candidate with the strongest electoral prospects to defeat the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) in the 2027 general election. Makinde, who confirmed that he was actively involved in discussions over a possible opposition alliance, declared his willingness to work with either former Vice President Atiku Abubakar or the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Peter Obi, if the arrangement offered the best chance of defeating the ruling party. Speaking in an exclusive interview with ARISE News, the Governor said the choice of a candidate should be determined by data, manifestos, past performance and the sentiments of Nigerians rather than personal preference. “We’re still discussing,” he said. Asked directly whether he was open to an alliance with other leading opposition figures, Makinde answered in the affirmative. “Not only that I’m open, we’re actively discussing this,” he said. He declined to say whether he would prefer an arrangement with Atiku or Obi, arguing that such a consequential political decision should be based on evidence. “To arrive at a decision, you need data,” he said. “We just won’t say, ‘Oh, okay,’ take emotional decision and say, ‘Oh, it’s you.’ We have manifestos now, we have certain things in that manifesto. We will sit down, we have maybe historical performance. We also have the sentiment of the people. All of those things will come together and arrive at a decision.” Makinde drew on his background in the oil and gas industry to explain how political rivals could become partners when their interests and capabilities aligned. Asked specifically whether he would work with Atiku if available data showed that the former vice president was the strongest candidate around whom the opposition should coalesce. “Yes,” Makinde replied. “I’m willing to work with any Nigerian.” The Governor also invoked the 1999 presidential election, noting that Olu Falae performed overwhelmingly well in the South-west but could not translate his regional strength into a national victory. “Our biggest challenge is, first, to agree on what is the best course of action, and then seek an alliance,” he said. He also pointed to South Africa’s experience of political cooperation as evidence that competing political forces could negotiate an arrangement when circumstances demanded it. “That negotiation will not be anything personal,” Makinde said. “That negotiation will be the deal for Nigeria, by Nigeria.” That personal ambitions should not prevent opposition figures from adopting a common electoral strategy. He said the APM has the backing of most of the Peoples Democratic Party’s (PDP) political structure as he prepared to contest the presidency in 2027. The APM presidential candidate said the party’s strength partly derived from the political structure that supported his emergence as Oyo State governor under the PDP, despite the internal challenges that affected the opposition party. “Remember, I became Governor under PDP. Remember, we had issues within PDP. But majority of the PDP structure, they’re actually with us in APM.” He confirmed that the APM was a faction of the PDP when the interviewer asked whether his party was relying on the PDP structure. “Yes, it’s a faction of the PDP,” he said. He described the APM as a relatively new party but argued that its age would not prevent it from making a strong showing in the 2027 presidential election. “APM is relatively new,” he said. Makinde also cited the performances of the Labour Party and the New Nigeria Peoples Party (NNPP) in the 2023 election to support his argument that a party with a limited electoral history could attract significant votes. “Labour Party in 2019, throughout the country, had 6,000 votes. 6,000 and some. In 2023, Peter Obi moved into Labour Party. No governor, no senator, no big politician. And he was able to move Labour Party’s vote from 6,000 four years earlier to 6 million plus in 2023,” he said. He also referenced the NNPP’s performance after former Kano State Governor, Rabiu Kwankwaso, joined the party. “Four years earlier, they were right around 6,000 plus also nationally. And former governor Rabiu Kwankwaso moved into NNPP. And the share of votes went from 6,000 to 1.4 million votes.” Challenged on the comparison, given that Obi had been a vice-presidential candidate in 2019 and Kwankwaso had previously contested the presidency, Makinde maintained that his own political journey showed that a candidate did not necessarily need a long record in public office to build electoral support. “If you read my trajectory to becoming the governor of Oyo State, this is my very first job in the public sector.” The governor also defended his decision to seek the presidency, arguing that the country needed fundamental changes in the way it was governed rather than gradual policy adjustments. He criticised Tinubu’s administration over electricity, saying: “The president promised that, look, I will fix electricity. Nigerians believed him. Has electricity been fixed?” Makinde said he believed the country was underachieving and that incremental reforms would not address its problems. “They don’t seem to be working. We’re underachieving. As a matter of fact, we have to completely change the game.” He also rejected arguments that improvements in the economy at the macroeconomic level would eventually benefit ordinary Nigerians, saying the government should be judged by the impact of its policies on households. “If you’re saying, oh, things are happening at the macro level, but it will filter down to micro, I see those as just excuses and shifting blimps.” Makinde questioned whether Nigerians were experiencing relief from the rising cost of living and whether families could afford their basic needs. “What’s the impact on the ordinary people on the streets? Are Nigerians hungry? Are more families able to, you know, afford certain things?” he asked. Makinde scored Tinubu’s administration 34 per cent, while acknowledging progress on state police and student financing but insisting that the government had fallen short of what Nigeria required. “It’s just about the same percentage of the people that supported him in 2023. Thirty-four per cent,” he said. The governor argued that Tinubu’s challenge went beyond implementing individual policies to building sufficient national support for his government’s programmes. “You need the 67 per cent of Nigerians that were against him in 2023 to be on board,” he said. “This is a massive number.” On the push for state police, which he has long advocated as part of his argument for bringing security decisions closer to communities, Makinde gave Tinubu credit for advancing the proposal. “The President has done well with the formation of the state police,” he said. He, however, argued that state policing should not necessarily be introduced simultaneously across the federation. Instead, states capable of establishing their own police services should be allowed to proceed, while others could join when ready. He also offered qualified support for the Federal Government’s intervention in tertiary education through student financing, arguing that providing students with access to funds addressed only one part of a much broader challenge. “Having money for students to go to school… is a small fraction of what they’re supposed to do. You need the teachers that are motivated. You need even security” for educational institutions. He argued that reforms must ultimately ensure young Nigerians acquire the skills and knowledge required to secure employment or become entrepreneurs. Makinde said isolated interventions could represent progress without necessarily resolving the underlying problems. “If you have three or four pockets and one is being addressed, I would say it’s a movement in the right direction. But that alone will not solidly ensure that our children have skills and knowledge that can either make them employable or turn them into entrepreneurs.” He maintained that Nigeria needed a more coordinated approach to economic development, security, education and governance, presenting his proposed “Reset Nigeria” agenda as an alternative to the current administration. Makinde promised to publish a transparent petroleum pricing template, saying Nigerians should know exactly how pump prices were determined. He said Nigerians could pay significantly less for petroleum products, alleging corruption within the existing system and promising to make the country’s fuel pricing template public if elected president. He said transparency in petroleum pricing would be a priority from his first day in office. “I believe that there’s corruption within the system,” he said. The governor, who worked in the oil and gas industry before entering politics, said Nigerians should be able to see the components used to determine the prices they pay for petroleum products rather than being presented with a final figure without sufficient explanation. He said his administration would disclose the pricing template, allowing the public to understand the assumptions and costs behind pump prices. Pressed to state exactly how much Nigerians should expect to pay for petrol under his presidency, Makinde declined to give a specific figure but insisted that the price could be “significantly lower”. He said his position was informed by his professional experience in the petroleum industry, describing oil and gas as an area in which he had considerable technical expertise dating back to the early 1990s. He also questioned the long-running debate over fuel subsidy, recalling Tinubu’s position during the 2012 subsidy protests and arguing that inefficiencies and corruption within the petroleum system needed to be confronted. Makinde criticised the federal government’s management of the economy and the impact of national policy decisions on households and subnational governments. He said increased nominal revenues should not automatically be interpreted as improved prosperity because inflation and the depreciation of the naira had significantly increased the cost of wages, infrastructure and other government obligations. Using Oyo State as an example, Makinde said the state’s monthly salary bill had risen from about N4.5 billion when he assumed office in 2019 to approximately N18 billion. He argued that wages and government revenues should therefore be assessed in terms of purchasing power rather than nominal increases. Makinde also recalled that a 65-kilometre road awarded by his administration in 2019 cost less than N9 billion, saying comparable infrastructure would cost substantially more today. He said his economic programme would focus on improving purchasing power and productive capacity rather than relying on higher nominal government revenues as evidence of prosperity. He nevertheless insisted that greater transparency and the removal of corruption and inefficiencies from the system would result in Nigerians paying substantially less for fuel. Makinde accused the Tinubu administration of using the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) to pressure opposition governors into joining the APC, warning that the alleged practice threatened Nigeria’s multiparty democracy. He described the alleged political blackmail as an attempt to weaken opposition parties ahead of the presidential election, arguing that rather than seek the support of Nigerians who did not vote for the APC in the last presidential election, the ruling party had concentrated on attracting governors through coercion. “What we’ve seen is, well, okay, I have the governors, they come to APC. If you don’t, you will be blackmailed,” he said.
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/14/m.title_zh: 马金德：反对党必须结成联盟，支持最有希望赢得选举的候选人
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/14/m.body_zh: 奥约州州长、人民进步联盟（APM）总统候选人塞伊·马金德表示，未能履行成立联合政府的协议，已使奥约州与蒂努布断绝关系；反对党必须结成联盟，支持最有希望赢得选举的总统候选人，以便在2027年大选中击败执政的进步大会（APC）。马金德证实，他正积极参与有关反对派可能结盟的讨论，并表示，如果这样的安排能为击败执政党提供最佳机会，他愿意与前副总统阿提库·阿布巴卡或尼日利亚民主大会总统候选人彼得·奥比合作。在接受ARISE News独家采访时，这位州长说，候选人的选择应由数据、竞选纲领、过往表现和尼日利亚民众的意愿决定，而不是个人偏好。他说：“我们仍在讨论。”当被直接问及是否愿意与其他主要反对派人物结盟时，马金德给出了肯定答复。他说：“我不仅愿意，我们还在积极讨论此事。”他没有说明自己更倾向于与阿提库还是奥比达成安排，认为 Such a consequential political decision 应以证据为依据。他说：“要作出决定，你必须有数据。我们不能只说‘哦，好吧’，凭情绪作出决定，然后说‘哦，就是你’。我们现在有竞选纲领，纲领里会明确一些事项。我们会坐下来讨论，也许还会参考历史表现。我们也会了解民众的意愿。所有这些因素结合起来，才能作出决定。”马金德以自己在石油和天然气行业的经历为例，说明当政治对手的利益和能力相互契合时，如何成为合作伙伴。当被具体问及，如果现有数据显示前副总统是最有能力吸引反对派团结支持的候选人，他是否愿意与阿提库合作时，马金德回答：“愿意。”他说：“我愿意与任何尼日利亚人合作。”这位州长还提请人们注意1999年总统选举，称奥卢·法拉赫在西南地区的表现极为出色，但未能把地区优势转化为全国性胜利。他说：“我们面临的最大挑战，首先是就最佳行动方案达成一致，然后寻求结盟。”他还以南非政治合作的经验作为例证，说明在情况需要时，竞争中的政治力量可以协商达成安排。马金德说：“这种协商不会涉及任何个人利益。这将是尼日利亚人为了尼日利亚达成的协议。”个人野心不应阻止反对派人物采取共同的选举策略。他说，在准备竞选2027年总统职位时，APM获得了人民民主党（PDP）大部分政治架构的支持。这位APM总统候选人表示，尽管该党内部面临挑战，但该党的力量部分来自支持他在PDP时期成为奥约州州长的政治架构。他说：“别忘了，我是在PDP时期成为州长的。也别忘了，PDP内部曾有问题。但PDP架构中的多数人实际上都支持我们，加入了APM。”当采访者询问其政党是否依靠PDP的政治架构时，他确认APM当时是PDP的一个派系。他说：“是的，它是PDP的一个派系。”他把APM描述为一个相对较新的政党，但认为党龄不会妨碍该党在2027年总统选举中取得亮眼成绩。他说：“APM是一个相对较新的政党。”马金德还引用工党和新尼日利亚人民党（NNPP）在2023年选举中的表现，以支持他的论点，即选举历史较短的政党也可能吸引大量选票。他说：“工党在2019年于全国获得了6,000票，6,000多票。2023年，彼得·奥比加入工党。没有州长，没有参议员，也没有大政治家，但他仍能把工党的得票从四年前的6,000票提高到2023年的600多万票。”他还提到前卡诺州州长拉比乌·夸恩克瓦索加入NNPP后该党的表现。他说：“四年前，该党在全国的票数也只有约6,000多票。后来前州长拉比乌·夸恩克瓦索加入NNPP，得票从6,000票升至140万票。”尽管奥比在2019年曾担任副总统候选人、夸恩克瓦索也曾竞选总统，马金德在比较二人时仍坚持认为，他自己的政治历程说明，候选人不一定需要长期公职履历才能建立选举支持。他说：“如果你了解我成为奥约州州长的经历，那是我在公共部门的第一份工作。”这位州长还为竞选总统的决定辩护，认为国家需要的是彻底改变治理方式，而不是逐步调整政策。他批评蒂努布政府的供电情况，说：“总统承诺过，听着，我会解决电力问题。尼日利亚人相信了他。电力问题解决了吗？”马金德认为，国家的表现低于预期渐进式改革无法解决现有问题。他说：“这些做法似乎没有奏效。我们的表现低于预期。事实上，我们必须彻底改变游戏规则。”他还驳斥了有关宏观经济改善最终会使普通尼日利亚人受益的说法，认为政府应以政策对家庭的影响来评判。他说：“如果你说‘哦，宏观层面正在发生变化，之后会传导到微观层面’，在我看来，这不过是借口和推卸责任。”马金德质疑生活成本上涨是否给尼日利亚人带来缓解，以及家庭是否负担得起基本生活需求。他问：“这对街上的普通人有什么影响？尼日利亚人挨饿了吗？更多家庭能够负担某些东西了吗？”马金德给蒂努布政府的评分为34%，同时承认州级警察和學生资助取得了一些进展，但坚称政府仍未达到尼日利亚的需要。他说：“这基本上与2023年支持他的民众比例相同，34%。”这位州长认为，蒂努布面临的挑战不只是落实各项政策，而是为其政府计划建立足够的全国支持。他说：“你需要2023年反对他的那67%的尼日利亚人支持你的政策。这是一个庞大的数字。”对于推动建立州级警察——他长期主张把安全决策拉近社区——马金德肯定了蒂努布在推进该提议方面所做的努力。他说：“总统在组建州级警察方面做得很好。”不过他认为，联邦各地不一定应同时引入州级警察，而应允许具备条件组建自有警察服务的州先行推进，其他州可在准备就绪后再加入。他还对联邦政府通过学生资助干预高等教育的做法给予有条件支持，认为让学生获得资金只是解决更广泛挑战的一小部分。他说：“让学生有钱上学……只是他们应承担任务的一小部分。你需要有积极性的教师，还需要教育机构有安全保障。”他认为，改革最终必须确保尼日利亚年轻人获得就业或创业所需的技能和知识。马金德说，孤立的干预措施可以代表取得进展，却未必能解决根本问题。他说：“如果一个问题有三四块短板，而其中一块得到处理，我会说这是在朝正确方向迈进。但仅靠这一点，并不能切实确保我们的孩子拥有技能和知识，从而找到工作或成为企业家。”他坚持认为，尼日利亚在经济发展、安全、教育和治理方面需要采取协调程度更高的方法，并把他提出的“重置尼日利亚”议程作为现任政府的替代方案。马金德承诺公布透明的石油定价模板，称尼日利亚人应确切了解加油站价格是如何确定的。他说，尼日利亚人支付石油产品的费用可以大幅降低，并指称现行体系存在腐败，承诺如果当选总统，将公开该国的燃油定价模板。他说，石油定价透明度将是其上任首日的优先事项。他说：“我认为这套体系内存在腐败。”这位进入政界前曾在石油和天然气行业工作的州长说，尼日利亚人应能看到用于确定其石油产品支付价格的各种构成因素，而不是只得到一个缺乏充分解释的最终数字。他说，他的政府将公布定价模板，让公众了解加油站价格背后的假设和成本。在被追问其担任总统期间尼日利亚人应支付多少汽油费时，马金德拒绝给出具体数字，但坚称价格可以“大幅降低”。他说，这一立场源于他在石油行业的专业经验，并称自20世纪90年代初以来，自己在石油和天然气领域拥有相当丰富的技术专长。他还质疑长期围绕燃油补贴展开的辩论，回顾了蒂努布在2012年燃油补贴抗议期间的立场，并认为必须解决石油体系内的低效和腐败问题。马金德批评联邦政府管理经济的方式，以及国家政策决定对家庭和地方政府的实际影响。他说，名义收入的增加不应自动被解读为繁荣状况改善，因为通货膨胀和尼日利亚奈拉贬值已经大幅推高了工资、基础设施和其他政府义务的成本。马金德以奥约州为例说，该州每月的工资支出从他2019年上任时约N45亿增至约N180亿。因此，他主张评估工资和财政收入时应依据实际购买力，而不是名义增幅。马金德还回忆说，其政府在2019年获批的一条65公里公路造价不足N90亿，而如今同类基础设施的成本会高得多。他说，他的经济计划将着重提高购买力和生产能力，而不是把更高的政府名义收入当作繁荣的证据。不过，他仍坚持认为，提高透明度并清除体系中的腐败和低效，将使尼日利亚人大幅减少燃油支出。马金德指控蒂努布政府利用经济和金融犯罪委员会（EFCC）向反对派州长施压，迫使他们加入APC，并警告称，据称这种做法威胁尼日利亚的多党民主。他称这种所谓的政治勒索是在总统选举前削弱反对党的企图，认为执政党没有争取上次总统选举中未投票给APC的尼日利亚人，反而专注于通过胁迫手段吸纳州长。他说：“我们看到的是，‘好吧，我已经有了这些州长，他们加入APC。如果你不加入，就会遭到政治勒索。’

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/14/o.title: Ogun 2027: Court Orders INEC to Publish Adebutu as PDP Candidate, Says Commission Lacks Powers to Disqualify Him
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/14/o.summary: Justice Peter Lifu of a Federal High Court, Abuja, has held that the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) cannot on its own disqualify a candidate nominated by a political party for an election. Justice Lifu subsequently ordered the commission to immediately publish the name of Mr. Ladi Adebutu as candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in the 2027 governorship election in Ogun State.
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/14/o.summary_zh: 阿布贾联邦高等法院法官彼得·利富裁定，独立国家选举委员会（INEC）不能自行取消政党为选举提名的候选人资格。利富法官随后命令该委员会立即公布拉迪·阿德布图的姓名，将其列为人民民主党（PDP）在2027年奥贡州州长选举中的候选人。
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/14/o.body: Justice Peter Lifu of a Federal High Court, Abuja, has held that the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) cannot on its own disqualify a candidate nominated by a political party for an election. Justice Lifu subsequently ordered the commission to immediately publish the name of Mr. Ladi Adebutu as candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in the 2027 governorship election in Ogun State. Adebutu had approached the Federal High Court to challenge the exclusion of his name in the list of candidates for next year published by INEC. While arguing that the action of the electoral umpire was unlawful and illegal, Adebutu sought an order directing the commission to publish his name as candidate of the PDP in the next year’s governorship election in Ogun State. Among the issues the court resolved are: Whether the plaintiffs’ right to fair hearing was breached; whether INEC has the power to unilaterally disqualify Adebutu, and whether the defendant can remove the name of the candidate, among others. On issue one, the judge held that the right to fair hearing was fundamental in Nigeria’s jurisprudence. “It is a judicial or administrative hearing conducted by due process. Therefore, before a decision is taken over a person, such person must be afforded the right to fair hearing,” the court said. The judge held that the plaintiff’s right to fair hearing was breached by INEC. “When a right is vested in a person, such right cannot be taken away without hearing from the person. “Adebutu was not accorded the right to be heard before INEC took the decision. Therefore, the right to fair hearing of the plaintiff is breached,” the court ruled. On the second issue, the judge said the first plaintiff noted that the second plaintiff was duly nominated by the party and his name forwarded to the defendant. “I have taken a cursory look at the judgement of the Supreme Court. The Supreme Court did not give INEC the power to start omitting or removing names of members from a party. “INEC does not have the power to remove names or disqualify any candidate on its own. The power to disqualify a candidate after the name has been forwarded resides with the FHC or State high Court. “The commission lacks the power to disqualify any candidate. Even if INEC believes that the name of a candidate was omitted, the commission must approach the court that has the power to remove the name. “The power to nominate a candidate for an election exclusively belongs to a political party, and the exercise of that power is within a party,” the court said. According to Lifu, a primary election was held on May 24, where Adebutu was nominated, adding that INEC had a duty to monitor an election to ensure that it complied with the provisions of the law. He said the facts showed that the primary election was not defective and that Adebutu was validly nominated. The second issue was therefore also resolved against the defendant, INEC. The court said, “All issues such as nomination issues, publications, are all pre-election matters. Adebutu was declared the winner of the primary election on May 24. INEC did not raise any issue. “As far as I know, no person filed any suit to challenge Adebutu 14 days after the conduct of the poll. It was baffling that INEC waited until August. “This court has established that INEC lacks the power to disqualify any candidate. “INEC should have approached the court to disqualify the candidate but it waited until after four months to take the action. “If this is not resolved, there will be a day that INEC will disqualify a candidate a day to election. This must not be allowed. This would be an absurdity. “I resolve this issue in favour of the plaintiffs,” the judge held. He stated, “Section 77(6) says a party shall make the list of members available not later than 21 days before the election. “It is only members whose names are contained that can participate in an election and the plaintiffs said Adebutu participated and that his name is in the list. “INEC should have raised the issue that Adebutu did not participate in its monitoring reports. “The action of INEC makes it plausible that the name of the second plaintiff was contained in the list and that his serial number is 1536. The judge said the court was inclined to quash the decision of the defendant, noting that INEC acted beyond its power. He said the commission had failed to do the needful and the court would disregard the evidence of its DW1. “The evidence of PW1 remains unchallenged, and uncontroverted. PW1 said that the flash drive submitted was not the one INEC brought to court and that he only submitted a soft copy in a flash drive contrary to INEC’s claim. Justice Lifu noted that the first defendant’s witness said the name of Adebutu was not in the flash drive and later turned to say he was not the one that received the flash drive. “The law is trite that failure to call a material or vital witness is fatal to the case of the defendant,” he said. Justice Lifu stated, “Consequently, the case of the plaintiff succeeds and is meritorious. The defendant acted ultra vires. INEC has no power, either administratively or otherwise, to remove a name if a candidate was validly nominated by the owner. “The removal is unlawful, unconstitutional and of no effect.” The court declared that by virtue of the Electoral Act, INEC was bound to publish Adebutu’s name. It ordered INEC to rectify the list published on October 10, 2026, to reflect Adebutu’s name. The court also declared that INEC could not pronounce the result of the 2027 governorship election without the participation of the plaintiffs, or “the election shall be of no effect and unconstitutional”. Meanwhile, a chieftain of the Labour Party (LP), Mr. Abayomi Arabambi, has faulted the decision of Justice Lifu which recognised Adebutu as the PDP governorship candidate for the 2027 Ogun State election. According to Arabambi, the verdict raises fundamental questions concerning statutory compliance, judicial interpretation and the binding force of Supreme Court decisions. Arabambi who is the National Chairman, South West (LP) stated that besides constitutional provisions, Section 84 of the Electoral Act empowers INEC to “provide rules and regulations which shall govern” political parties. “If INEC is truly a regulator, it should be allowed to regulate. It cannot see political parties breaking the law, breaching the Electoral Act and flouting its regulations and be helpless. “What decisions like today’s decision mean is that INEC is just a clerical office, a mere clearing house for information, documents, and stakeholders in the electoral process – without the ability to identify breaches of law or compel compliance. That is contrary to the nature of INEC as a regulator,” Arabambi stated in an open letter to the Chief Justice of Nigeria, Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, who is also the Chairman of the National Judicial Council (NJC). The LP chieftain claimed that the judgement, as reported, appears to have elevated the internal autonomy of political parties above the mandatory provisions of Sections 77(4), (5), (6) and (7) of the Electoral Act, 2026. “Consequently, it is submitted that the mere production of a different membership register during litigation cannot, without proof of its timely submission to INEC, retrospectively validate an otherwise defective nomination. “More troubling is the reported evidence that the PDP’s National Organising Secretary admitted under cross-examination that Adebutu’s name was absent from the register submitted to INEC, attributing the non-submission of another register containing his name to an error of omission. “An admitted statutory default cannot ordinarily be cured by an explanation of administrative inadvertence. The reported controversy surrounding serial number 1536 in the competing registers further raises a serious evidential question. “If that serial number belonged to another individual in the register submitted to INEC, the trial court was required to resolve the discrepancy before treating the subsequently produced register as conclusive proof of statutory compliance. “Furthermore, the proposition that INEC lacks the power to disqualify candidates must not be confused with the commission’s statutory responsibility to verify compliance with electoral requirements and supreme court judgement. Political party autonomy is not a licence to disregard express legislative prescriptions. “The Supreme Court’s reported decision of September 24, 2026, upholding the validity of the relevant provisions of Section 77, makes it particularly important that those provisions receive their full legal effect and can be enforced,” he added. He subsequently urged the Court of Appeal to determine whether the trial court’s reasoning effectively permitted a political party to achieve through subsequent documentary production what Section 77(6) prohibits it from doing during the primary process. According to Arabambi, where a statute expressly requires a political party to use the membership register submitted to INEC, a court cannot dispense with that requirement merely because the party subsequently produces another register containing the name of its preferred candidate. “Any contrary approach risks converting mandatory electoral safeguards into optional administrative formalities,” he submitted. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/14/o.body_zh: 阿布贾联邦高等法院法官彼得·利夫裁定，独立国家选举委员会（INEC）不能仅凭自身决定取消政党提名的候选人的资格。利夫法官随后命令该委员会立即公布拉迪·阿德布图先生的姓名，将其列为人民民主党（PDP）在奥贡州2027年州长选举中的候选人。阿德布图曾向联邦高等法院起诉，质疑独立国家选举委员会公布的明年候选人名单为何将他排除在外。阿德布图主张，选举裁判机构的这一行为违法且不合法，并请求法院命令该委员会在奥贡州明年的州长选举中公布他为人民民主党候选人。法院审理并解决的问题包括：原告获得公平审理的权利是否受到侵犯；独立国家选举委员会有权否决定阿德布图的资格吗；被告能否删除候选人的姓名等。关于第一个问题，法官认为，公平审理权是尼日利亚判例法中的一项基本权利。法院表示：“公平审理是依照正当程序进行的司法或行政审理。因此，在就一个人的问题作出决定之前，必须给予该人享有公平审理的权利。”法官认定，独立国家选举委员会侵犯了原告的公平审理权。法院裁定：“当一项权利归属于某人时，未经听取该人的陈述，不得剥夺其权利。独立国家选举委员会在作出决定前，没有给予阿德布图陈述意见的权利。因此，原告的公平审理权受到了侵犯。”关于第二个问题，法官表示，第一名原告指出，第二名原告已由该党正式提名，其姓名也已报送被告。法院称：“我粗略查看了最高法院的判决。最高法院并未赋予独立国家选举委员会开始删除或剔除政党成员姓名的权力。独立国家选举委员会无权自行删除姓名或取消任何候选人的资格。在姓名报送之后，取消候选人资格的权力属于联邦高等法院或州高等法院。该委员会无权取消任何候选人的资格。即使独立国家选举委员会认为候选人的姓名被遗漏，也必须向有权删除该姓名的法院提出申请。提名候选人参选的权力完全属于政党，行使这项权力属于政党的内部事务。”据利夫介绍，5月24日举行了初选，阿德布图在初选中获得提名；他还说，独立国家选举委员会有责任监督选举，以确保选举符合法律规定。他说，事实表明初选不存在缺陷，阿德布图获得了有效提名。因此，第二个问题也被裁定对被告独立国家选举委员会不利。法院表示：“提名、公布等所有问题均属于选举前事项。阿德布图于5月24日被宣布为初选获胜者。独立国家选举委员会没有提出任何异议。据我所知，在投票结束14天内，没有任何人就阿德布图提起诉讼。独立国家选举委员会一直等到8月才行动，这令人费解。本院已经认定，独立国家选举委员会无权取消任何候选人的资格。独立国家选举委员会本应向法院申请取消该候选人的资格，却等到四个月后才采取行动。如果不解决这个问题，总有一天独立国家选举委员会会在选举日当天取消候选人的资格。这种情况绝不能被允许，否则将成为荒谬之事。我裁定这些问题有利于原告。”法官表示：“《选举法》第77条第(6)款规定，政党应最迟在选举前21天提供成员名单。只有列入名单的成员才能参加选举，而原告称阿德布图参加了选举，其姓名也在名单中。独立国家选举委员会本应提出阿德布图没有参加其监督报告所载活动的问题。独立国家选举委员会的行为使人可以合理推断，第二名原告的姓名确实列在名单中，其编号为1536。”法官表示，法院倾向于撤销被告的决定，并指出独立国家选举委员会越权行事。他说，该委员会没有履行必要职责，法院将不采纳其第一证人提交的证据。法院称：“第一证人的证据仍未受到质疑，也不存在相反证据。第一证人称，所提交的多闪存驱动器并非独立国家选举委员会带到法院的那个，他只是依照独立国家选举委员会的说法，提交了一份存有多闪存驱动器的电子副本。”利夫法官指出，第一被告的证人先称阿德布图的姓名不在多闪存驱动器中，后来又改口称自己并非接收多闪存驱动器的人。利夫法官表示：“法律早已明确，被告不出庭传唤重要或关键证人，属于对被告案件致命的程序过错。”利夫法官强调：“因此，原告的诉讼请求获得支持，且理由充分。被告越权行事。如果候选人的提名获得政党有效确认，独立国家选举委员会无论在行政上还是其他方面均无权删除其姓名。删除该姓名违法、违宪且不产生任何效力。”法院依据《选举法》宣布，独立国家选举委员会有义务公布阿德布图的姓名，并命令其更正2026年10月10日公布的名单，将阿德布图的姓名列入其中。法院还宣布，独立国家选举委员会若不在原告参与的情况下宣布2027年州长选举结果，该选举“将不产生效力并违宪”。与此同时，工党（LP）酋长阿巴约米·阿拉班比先生批评了利夫法官的判决。该判决承认阿德布图为奥贡州2027年选举的人民民主党州长候选人。阿拉班比表示，这一判决提出了有关依法行事、司法解释以及最高法院判决约束力等根本问题。身为工党西南地区全国主席的阿拉班比表示，除了宪法规定外，《选举法》第84条还授权独立国家选举委员会“制定管辖”政党的“规则和条例”。他表示：“如果独立国家选举委员会确实是一家监管机构，就应当允许其履行监管职责。它不能对政党违反法律、违反《选举法》以及无视其条例的行为袖手旁观。诸如今日判决这类决定意味着，独立国家选举委员会不过是一个 clerical office，一个仅负责为选举流程中的信息、文件和利益相关方办理传递的机构，无法识别违法情况或强制落实合规要求。这与独立国家选举委员会作为监管机构的性质相悖。”阿拉班比在致尼日利亚首席大法官、同时担任国家司法委员会（NJC）主席的库迪拉特·凯凯雷-埃库恩法官的公开信中作出了上述表示。这位工党酋长声称，据报道，该判决似乎将政党的内部自主权置于《2026年选举法》第77条第(4)、(5)、(6)和(7)款的强制性规定之上。他表示：“因此，必须指出，在诉讼期间仅提交另一份成员名册，在没有证据证明其已及时提交独立国家选举委员会的情况下，不能追溯性地使原本有缺陷的提名获得有效确认。更令人担忧的是，据报道的证据，人民民主党全国组织秘书在交叉询问中承认，阿德布图的姓名不在提交给独立国家选举委员会的名册中，并把未提交另一份载有其姓名的名册归因于遗漏错误。对于已承认的法定违规，通常不能以行政疏忽作为补救理由。据报道，围绕两个相互竞争的名册中编号1536所产生的争议，进一步提出了严重的证据问题。如果该编号在提交给独立国家选举委员会的名册中属于另一人，原审法院就必须在把后来提交的名册视为符合法定要求的决定性证据之前解决这一差异。此外，独立国家选举委员会无权取消候选人资格的命题，不能与该委员会核验选举要求及最高法院判决是否得到遵守的法定责任混为一谈。政党自主权并非无视明确立法规定的许可。”他补充道：“据报道，最高法院于2026年9月24日作出判决，确认《选举法》第77条相关条款有效，因此，确保这些条款得到充分法律效力并得到执行显得尤为重要。”此后，他敦促上诉法院裁定，原审法院的推理是否实际上允许政党通过事后提交文件，实现《选举法》第77条第(6)款在初选过程中所禁止的行为。阿拉班比表示，当法律明确要求政党使用提交给独立国家选举委员会的成员名册时，法院不能仅仅因为该党后来提交了另一份载有其属意候选人姓名的名册，就免除这一要求。他表示：“任何相反做法，都有可能把强制性选举保障措施变成可有可无的行政形式。”THISDAY于1995年1月22日创刊，由THISDAY https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/14/u.summary_zh: 伊莫州州长霍普·乌佐迪马表示，要减少尼日利亚的大规模贫困，必须在农村社区创造就业机会，因为全国80%的贫困人口生活在这些社区。乌佐迪马在以“未来在于地方：激发基层经济以实现包容性增长”为主题的讲话中表示，尽管政府无法为民众创造足够的就业岗位，但必须营造有利的环境，吸引私营部门投资并创造所需就业。
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/14/u.body: The Governor of Imo State, Hope Uzodimma, has said that reducing mass poverty in Nigeria requires the creation of jobs in rural communities, which are home to 80 per cent of the country’s poor. The governor made this known yesterday in Lagos while speaking as the guest speaker at the Lagos Country Club’s “Policy Dialogue with Government Leaders”. Speaking on the theme, “The Future Is Local: Stimulating Grassroots Economies for Inclusive Growth”, Uzodimma said while government could not create enough jobs for the people, it must provide an enabling environment to attract private sector investment and create the jobs needed. He noted that Nigerian cities had become saturated as people continued to leave rural communities for urban centres, which lacked the capacity to create enough jobs to meet the growing demand. “Things get complicated when people move faster than cities can create jobs, and when the places they leave are abandoned rather than developed,” he said. The governor said the solution was to create an enabling environment in rural communities where small and medium-scale businesses could thrive. He warned that this had become imperative given the continuous growth in the population of young Nigerians in need of jobs. “In our own country, neglected places have expressed their frustration at the ballot box and through far more dangerous means. A local economy that gives young people a stake in peace is among the best security investments a government can make. “Rural areas hold 80 per cent of the country’s poor. When local economies sit idle, the consequences do not stay local. Young people leave for the big cities or stay behind with nothing productive to do. That idleness has a way of finding the wrong employers. Crime and insecurity feed on it,” Uzodimma emphasised. He noted that a poor state had little to tax and, therefore, relied increasingly on allocations from Abuja and the few cities capable of generating sufficient revenue to sustain themselves. Uzodimma said government must provide the necessary infrastructure to enable small business operators to succeed in rural communities, noting that this would help address unemployment in the country. “The most recent national survey of micro, small and medium enterprises, carried out by the Small and Medium Enterprises Development Agency of Nigeria (SMEDAN) and the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS), found close to 40 million such businesses. Together they account for nearly half of GDP and create close to nine in every ten jobs. Most are small, informal and far from Lagos, held back by unreliable power, scarce and expensive finance, poor roads, multiple taxation and the high cost of dealing with government. Every improvement to the foundations goes straight to their bottom line. “Foundations matter only when someone builds on them, and in a market economy that someone is the private investor. Government should not try to pick winners. It should lower the cost and risk of doing business and then make it easy for capital to find opportunities that already exist. That is the purpose of the Orashi Special Energy Free Zone in Ohaji/Egbema (created by the state government), which holds a ten-year operating licence from the Oil and Gas Free Zones Authority and an approved master plan, so that investors in gas and energy can process and add value close to the resource,” he said. The governor also said his administration had sought to make local economies work by laying the necessary foundations, supporting local enterprises and investing in the people, but acknowledged that much remained to be done. He reiterated that private capital would not flow into areas where basic infrastructure was lacking, stressing that the first responsibility of any state seeking grassroots economic growth was to provide such infrastructure. “Power is the constraint every business in Nigeria knows best. The constitutional and legal reforms of 2023 allowed states to regulate their own electricity markets, and we decided not to wait. In February, as part of our Imo State at 50 celebrations, we commissioned the first phase of the Orashi Power Project under our Light Up Imo programme. It is run by our indigenous Orashi Electricity Company with its technical partner, Madkour Holding of Egypt, and includes a 15 MVA injection substation and a new distribution network on the Owerri axis,” he added. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/14/u.title_zh: 乌佐迪马：政府必须与私营部门合作，创造农村就业机会并消除贫困
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/14/u.body_zh: 伊莫州州长霍普·乌佐迪马表示，要减少尼日利亚（国家，首都阿布贾）的大规模贫困，必须在农村社区创造就业机会，因为全国80%的贫困人口生活在那里。州长昨天在拉各斯出席拉各斯乡村俱乐部“与政府领导人政策对话”活动并担任主讲嘉宾时透露了这一点。乌佐迪马在以“未来在于地方：激发基层经济，实现包容性增长”为主题发言时表示，尽管政府无法为人民创造足够的就业岗位，但必须提供有利的环境，吸引私营部门投资并创造所需岗位。他指出，随着人们不断离开农村社区前往城市中心，尼日利亚（国家，首都阿布贾）的城市已经变得饱和，而这些城市缺乏创造足够岗位以满足日益增长需求的能力。他说：“当人口流动速度超过城市创造岗位的速度，而他们离开的地方不是得到开发而是被遗弃时，事情就会变得复杂。”州长表示，解决办法是在农村社区创造有利的环境，让小企业和中型企业能够蓬勃发展。他警告称，鉴于尼日利亚（国家，首都阿布贾）年轻人口持续增长且亟需就业，这项任务已经变得至关重要。他说：“在我们自己的国家，被遗忘的地方已经在投票箱前，并通过更加危险的方式表达不满。让年轻人参与和平进程的本地经济，是政府能够作出的最佳安全投资之一。“农村地区居住着全国80%的贫困人口。当本地经济停滞不前时，其后果不会仅限于当地。年轻人要么前往大城市，要么留在原地、无所事事。这种闲置状态往往会让他们找到错误的雇主。犯罪和治安问题由此滋生。”乌佐迪马强调。他指出，贫穷的州几乎没有税收来源，因此越来越依赖阿布贾以及少数能够创造足够收入维持自身运转的城市拨款。乌佐迪马表示，政府必须提供必要的基础设施，使小微企业在农村社区取得成功，并指出这将有助于缓解尼日利亚（国家，首都阿布贾）的失业问题。他说：“尼日利亚（国家，首都阿布贾）中小企业发展局（SMEDAN）和国家统计局（NBS）最近开展的一项关于微型企业、小型和中型企业的全国调查发现，此类企业接近4000万家。它们合计贡献了近一半的国内生产总值，并创造了近九成十的就业岗位。大多数企业规模小、属于非正规经营，而且远离拉各斯，受到电力供应不稳定、融资稀缺且成本高昂、道路状况不佳、多重征税以及与政府打交道成本过高的拖累。基础条件每得到一项改善，都会直接改善它们的收益。“只有有人在这些基础条件之上建设，它们才具有意义。在市场经济中，这个人就是私人投资者。政府不应试图挑选赢家，而应降低经营成本和风险，让资本很容易找到已经存在的机会。这正是奥拉希特别能源自由区在奥希/埃格贝马设立的目的。该自由区由州政府创建，持有一份有效期为10年的石油和天然气自由区管理局运营许可证，并拥有获批的总体规划，以便天然气和能源投资者能够在资源所在地附近加工并提升附加值。”他说。州长还表示，其政府已通过铺设必要基础设施、支持本地企业和投资于民来推动本地经济发展，但承认仍有大量工作要做。他重申，私人资本不会流向缺乏基本基础设施的地区，并强调，任何寻求基层经济增长的州，首要责任都是提供这类基础设施。他说：“电力是尼日利亚（国家，首都阿布贾）每家企业都深有体会的制约因素。2023年的宪法和法律改革允许各州监管自己的电力市场，而我们决定不能等待。今年2月，作为伊莫州成立50周年庆典的一部分，我们启动了“点亮伊莫”计划下的奥拉希电力项目第一阶段。该项目由我们本土的奥拉希电力公司运营，其技术合作伙伴是埃及的Madkour Holding，项目包括一座15兆伏安注入式变电站，以及奥韦里轴线上的新配电网络。”他补充道。THISDAY创刊于1995年1月22日，由THISDAY NEWSPAPERS LTD.出版，地址为尼日利亚（国家，首都阿布贾）拉各斯阿帕帕溪路35号，在尼日利亚（国家，首都阿布贾）36个州、联邦首都辖区以及世界各地设有办公室。该报是尼日利亚（国家，首都阿布贾）最具权威性的新闻媒体，通过所有平台面向政治、商业、专业和外交精英以及更广泛的中产阶级，同时为有抱负者和千禧一代提供新思想、文化与技术的交汇点。该报秉持公共信托精神，致力于追求真理与理性，报道范围涵盖突发新闻、政治、商业、金融市场、艺术、体育和社区等议题，直至人与社会的交汇点。您可以给我们发送电子邮件：hello@thisdaylive.com，或访问我们的联系我们页面

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/14/2.body: The governorship candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Kwara State for next year’s general elections, Prof. Abdulmumin Ajia, has said that his administration would introduce a minimum wage of N120,000 for workers in the state public service if elected as the next governor of the state. While the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) senatorial candidate for Kwara South Senatorial district in Kwara State for 2027 polls, Hon. Saheed Popoola, yesterday, pledged to prioritise security, infrastructure, agriculture, youth empowerment and healthcare if elected during the polls. Prof. Ajia also proposed a system-driven administration anchored on accountability, institutional efficiency and reduced government expenditure. Ajia made the submissions yesterday during an engagement organised by the Correspondents’ Chapel of the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ) Kwara State Council, under its ‘News Keg’ series with governorship candidates, held at the chapel’s secretariat in Ilorin, the state capital. The university don said his proposed administration would prioritise strong and predictable government institutions rather than concentrate governance around an individual. He stressed that improved public sector efficiency, reduced wastage and strategic partnerships with the private sector would help generate resources for workers’ welfare and development. He argued that state governments should have the flexibility to determine workers’ salaries according to their financial capacity, provided they did not pay below the minimum wage prescribed by the federal government. “The federal government can just give minimum wage so that in Nigeria, we cannot pay less than N120,000. If I want to pay N200,000, that’s my business, if I can pay it,” Ajia said. He criticised what he described as excessive federal control over wage administration, maintaining that states should be allowed to determine their remuneration structures within their financial capabilities. The NDC candidate also expressed readiness to challenge existing regulatory arrangements through legal means where necessary, arguing that constitutional responsibilities of state governments should be respected. Explaining his proposed governance model, Ajia said his administration would introduce clearly defined responsibilities, measurable performance targets and specific timelines across ministries, departments and agencies to ensure accountability in public service delivery. “What’s going to make the future government different is that I’m going to invest in systems. “I don’t want to build the government around myself. I want to build the government around predictable systems,” he stated. Using the process of obtaining government licences as an example, he said applications should be processed within stipulated periods, with appropriate sanctions for public officials who fail to meet established deadlines without reasonable justification. He added that civil servants would be assigned clear responsibilities and measurable expectations similar to the private sector where employees are assessed based on their ability to deliver agreed targets within specified timelines. According to him, building a government around functional institutions rather than personalities would strengthen accountability, improve service delivery and create a more predictable environment for businesses and residents. Earlier, the Chairman of the News Keg Committee, Ibrahim Alege, represented by a former chairman of the Correspondents’ Chapel, Mallam Abdulhakeem Garba, challenged governorship candidates in the state to move beyond political slogans and campaign promises by presenting practical and achievable plans for addressing Kwara’s development challenges. Alege said the News Keg initiative was established to provide a platform for direct interaction between journalists and public figures, allowing political actors to explain their programmes and respond to questions on issues affecting the people. He stressed that with the 2027 governorship election approaching, voters deserved to know not only what candidates intended to achieve but also how they planned to translate their promises into measurable results. “Beyond political slogans and campaign promises, the people deserve to know what each candidate intends to do differently, how they plan to achieve their objectives and how their proposed policies will address the challenges confronting the state,” he said. He urged Ajia and other governorship hopefuls to provide detailed explanations of their proposed policies, particularly in critical sectors such as security, education, healthcare, infrastructure, agriculture, employment generation and economic development. The News Keg chairman also emphasised the responsibility of journalists to hold political actors accountable through professional, fair and objective engagement, noting that questions from reporters would be guided by public interest. “News Keg is not a political platform for endorsing any candidate or party. It is an independent media engagement initiative that provides equal opportunity for political actors to communicate their ideas to the people,” he added. The Chairman of the Correspondents’ Chapel, Alhaji Biola Azeez, also acknowledged Ajia’s presence at the engagement. The News Keg series is an initiative of the Kwara State Correspondents’ Chapel of the NUJ designed to bring journalists and influential public figures together to discuss issues of public interest, particularly as political activities gather momentum ahead of the 2027 general elections. Meanwhile, the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) senatorial candidate for Kwara South Senatorial district in Kwara State for 2027 polls, Hon. Popoola, a former Chairman of Offa Local Government Area made the pledge yesterday during the News Keg Engagement Series at the Correspond Chapel of the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ) in Ilorin. He outlined his agenda for the district, noting that the deteriorating security situation and inadequate infrastructure had continued to undermine economic development and residents’ well-being. He said his 27 years of political experience had equipped him with the knowledge and capacity to address the challenges facing the people. The candidate, who described himself as a grassroots politician, said he joined the PDP because of his conviction that the party had greater concern for the welfare of the masses. He expressed concern over the increasing cases of kidnapping in Kwara South, noting that residents could no longer move freely or go to their farms without fear of attacks. He recalled that communities in the district were previously relatively safe, adding that the current situation had created fear among farmers and other residents. Popoola said security would be his first priority, promising to facilitate stronger collaboration between communities and security agencies. He said he would replicate the neighbourhood watch initiative he established while serving as a local government chairman, which he described as effective in maintaining security in his area. According to him, the initiative will involve youths, Fulani residents and other community stakeholders, with members properly equipped and registered with the government. He added that he would also deploy his personal resources to support the initiative, stressing that local residents understood their communities better than security personnel deployed from other parts of the country. Popoola, a two-term member of the State House of Assembly, said he would use his legislative position to lobby the federal and state governments and relevant agencies to address security and infrastructure challenges in the district. On infrastructure, Popoola lamented the poor condition of roads linking communities in the district, particularly the Iloffa-Ekiti axis. He pledged to lobby relevant federal agencies for the rehabilitation and construction of major roads, including the Ilorin-Omu-Aran-Egbe and Ajase-Offa routes. He explained that lobbying was an important responsibility of legislators, adding that senators could facilitate development projects through effective engagement with government institutions. Popoola, who said he had served as a local government chairman, commissioner and member of the Kwara State House of Assembly twice, described experience as essential in effective representation. He also said he served as Secretary of the Governing Council of Kwara State Polytechnic between 2003 and 2007. The candidate further identified agriculture as a major economic opportunity for the district, given its vast arable land. He, however, stressed that addressing insecurity was necessary to enable farmers to return to their farms and boost food production. He expressed concern that kidnapping had disrupted farming activities, worsened food insecurity and exposed rural communities to economic hardship. Popoola narrated an incident in Isanlu-Isin where a farmer and his two children were reportedly abducted, saying he contributed N2 million towards efforts to secure their release. He alleged that the community had struggled to raise the ransom demanded by the kidnappers, while the local government contributed N50,000. He also alleged that another kidnapping incident involving a father and his two children occurred in Oro, calling on the state government to explain its efforts to address insecurity in the district. The PDP candidate urged the media to give adequate attention to security challenges in rural communities, noting that several incidents were not being reported. On youth development, he said unemployment and lack of empowerment opportunities could expose young people to criminal activities. He pledged to promote employment and empowerment programmes to engage youths and discourage their involvement in criminal activities. Popoola also promised to establish an office in each of the local government areas in Kwara South to improve communication and facilitate effective representation. He said the offices would serve as collection centres for complaints and development needs from the 83 wards in the senatorial district. According to him, each ward will have a legislative aide who will collate reports and forward them through liaison officers at the local government level. On healthcare, Popoola promised to facilitate improvements in the health sector, particularly the rehabilitation and revitalisation of non-functional cottage hospitals across the district. He said effective representation required a legislator who remained accessible and responsive to the needs of constituents. “I am going to be a listening senator. I will make myself available at all times,” he said. Popoola urged residents to consider candidates’ experience, competence and track records rather than being swayed solely by financial inducements during elections. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/14/2.title_zh: 2027年：夸拉州国家民主大会党州长候选人阿吉亚承诺向工人支付最低工资12万奈拉
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/14/2.body_zh: 尼日利亚民主大会党（NDC）在夸拉州参加明年大选的州长候选人阿布杜敏·阿贾亚教授表示，如果当选为该州下一任州长，他的政府将把州公共部门工作人员的最低工资提高到12万奈拉。与此同时，夸拉州夸拉南选区参加2027年选举的人民民主党（PDP）参议员候选人萨希德·波普拉先生昨天承诺，如果当选，他将优先处理安全、基础设施、农业、青年赋权和医疗卫生事务。阿贾亚教授还提出实行以问责、制度效率和减少政府开支为核心的制度化治理模式。阿贾亚昨天在尼日利亚记者协会（NUJ）夸拉州理事会记者团举办的“News Keg”州长候选人系列交流活动上作出上述表态，活动地点设在州首府伊洛林记者团秘书处。这位大学教授说，他提出的政府将优先建设强有力且可预测的政府机构，而不是围绕个人集中治理权。他强调，提高公共部门效率、减少浪费以及与私营部门建立战略伙伴关系，将有助于为工作人员的福祉和发展创造资源。他认为，州政府应当拥有根据自身财政能力确定工作人员薪酬的灵活性，但不得支付低于联邦政府规定的最低工资。阿贾亚说：“联邦政府只需规定最低工资，确保在尼日利亚我们不能支付低于12万奈拉的工资。如果我想支付20万奈拉，那是我自己的事，只要我付得起。”他批评联邦政府过度控制工资管理，坚持州政府应获准在自身财政能力范围内确定薪酬结构。这位NDC候选人还表示，必要时准备通过法律途径挑战现行监管安排，认为州政府的宪法职责应得到尊重。在解释其治理模式时，阿贾亚表示，政府将为各部门、厅局和机构明确职责、设定可衡量的绩效指标并规定具体期限，以确保公共服务中的问责。他说：“未来政府之所以不同，是因为我要投资于制度。我不想围绕个人建设政府，我想围绕可预测的制度建设政府。”他以政府许可证审批程序为例，称申请应在规定期限内处理，对于无合理理由未能遵守既定期限的公职人员，应采取适当制裁措施。他补充说，公务员将被分配明确职责和可衡量的预期目标，效仿私营部门根据员工在规定期限内完成约定目标的能力进行评估的做法。他认为，围绕运转良好的机构而非个人建立政府，将强化问责、改善服务交付，并为企业居民营造更可预测的环境。News Keg委员会主席易卜拉欣·阿莱格此前由记者团前主席马拉姆·阿卜杜勒哈基姆·加尔巴代表，他敦促该州州长候选人超越政治口号和竞选承诺，提出切实可行且能够实现的计划，以应对夸拉州的发展挑战。阿莱格表示，News Keg倡议的设立旨在为记者与公众人物提供直接交流的平台，让政治人物能够阐述其政策纲领，并就影响民众的问题回答提问。他强调，随着2027年州长选举临近，选民不仅应了解候选人打算实现什么，还应了解他们计划如何把承诺转化为可衡量的成果。他说：“政治口号和竞选承诺之外，民众还应知道每位候选人打算采取何种不同做法、如何实现目标，以及其政策将如何应对该州面临的挑战。”他敦促阿贾亚和其他州长竞选者详细说明所提政策，特别是在安全、教育、医疗卫生、基础设施、农业、就业创造和经济发展等关键领域。News Keg主席还强调，记者有责任通过专业、公平和客观的交流对政治人物进行问责，并指出记者提出的问题将以公共利益为导向。他补充说：“News Keg不是为任何候选人或政党背书的政治平台。它是一项独立媒体交流倡议，为政治人物提供平等机会，让其向民众传达理念。”记者团主席阿哈吉·比奥拉·阿泽兹也确认阿贾亚出席了此次交流活动。News Keg系列活动由NUJ夸拉州记者团发起，旨在让记者和重要公众人物聚在一起讨论公共利益问题，尤其是在2027年大选前政治活动日益活跃之际。与此同时，夸拉州夸拉南选区参加2027年选举的PDP参议员候选人波普拉先生昨天在伊洛林NUJ记者团举办的News Keg交流系列活动上作出承诺。波普拉曾任奥法地方政府主席，他在活动中概述了该选区的施政议程，指出安全局势恶化和基础设施不足持续削弱经济发展及居民福祉。他说，自己27年的政治经历使其具备解决民众面临挑战的知识和能力。这位自称基层政治人物的候选人表示，他之所以加入PDP，是因为坚信该党更加关注广大民众的福祉。他对夸拉南地区绑架案件日益增多表示担忧，称居民如今出行或前往农场都不得不再遭袭击的恐惧。他提到，该选区各社区此前相对安全，而当前局势已令农民和其他居民陷入恐惧。波普拉说，安全将是他的首要任务，他承诺促进社区与安全机构之间更紧密的合作。他将复制自己担任地方政府主席期间建立的社区守望计划，并称该计划在维护其所在地区安全方面成效显著。他说，该计划将由青年、福拉尼族居民及其他社区利益相关者参与，成员将获得适当装备并向政府登记。他补充说，自己还将投入个人资源支持该计划，并强调当地居民比从全国其他地区部署的安全人员更了解各自社区。波普拉曾连续两届担任州议会议员。他说，将利用自己的立法职位游说联邦政府和州政府及相关机构，解决该选区的安全和基础设施问题。在基础设施方面，波普拉对该区连接各社区的道路状况糟糕表示遗憾，特别是伊洛法—埃基蒂路段。他承诺游说相关联邦机构整修和新建主要道路，包括伊洛林—奥穆—阿兰—埃格贝线和阿贾塞—奥法线路。他解释说，游说是议员的一项重要职责，议员可以通过与政府机构有效互动推动发展项目。波普拉曾任地方政府主席、州专员以及两届夸拉州议会议员，他说，经验对于有效代表选民至关重要。他还表示，自己曾于2003年至2007年担任夸拉州理工学院理事会秘书。这位候选人还指出，鉴于该选区拥有大片可耕地，农业是重要的经济机遇。但他强调，解决安全问题十分必要，只有这样农民才能返回田地并提高粮食产量。他对绑架活动扰乱农业生产、加剧粮食不安全并使农村社区陷入经济困境表示担忧。波普拉讲述了一起发生在伊桑卢—伊辛的事件，据称一名农民及其两个孩子遭到绑架；他说，自己为营救他们捐出了200万奈拉。他称，该社区筹措绑匪要求的赎金十分艰难，而地方政府仅出资5万奈拉。他还指称，奥罗地区发生了另一起父亲与两个孩子遭绑架的事件，并要求州政府说明其为解决该区安全问题所做的工作。PDP候选人敦促媒体充分关注农村社区的安全挑战，指出多起事件并未得到报道。在青年发展方面，他说，失业和缺乏赋权机会可能使年轻人铤而走险。他承诺推动就业和赋权项目，让青年参与其中并减少其卷入犯罪活动。波普拉还承诺在夸拉南各地方政府设立办公室，以改善沟通并促进有效代表。他说，这些办公室将作为该参议员选区83个选区反映意见和汇总发展需求的收集中心。他表示，每个选区都将配备一名立法助理，负责汇总报告，并通过地方政府层面的联络官转交。在医疗卫生方面，波普拉承诺推动改善该地区卫生部门的工作，尤其是整修和振兴全地区无法正常运营的小型医院。他说，有效代表需要一名始终能够接近选民并及时回应选民需求的议员。他说：“我要做一名倾听民意的参议员。我会随时让大家能够找到我。”波普拉敦促居民在选举时考虑候选人的经验、能力和履绩，而不是仅受金钱诱惑所左右。THISDAY于1995年1月22日创办，由THISDAY https://www.yna.co.kr/view/akr2026111401.title: 경찰, 박상용 검사 '李대통령 무고' 고발된 사건 공수처로 이첩
https://www.yna.co.kr/view/akr2026111401.summary: (서울=연합뉴스) 정지수 기자 = 쌍방울 대북송금 사건을 수사하며 이화영 전 경기도 평화부지사에게 허위 진술을 유도해 이재명 대통령을 무고했다는 의혹으로 고발된 박상용 인천지방공소청 부부장검사 사건이 고위공직자범죄수사처(공수처)로 이첩됐다. 14일 경찰에 따르면 서울 영등포경찰서는 박 검사의 무고·직권남용 권리행사방해 혐의 사건을 이달 6일 공수처로 이첩했다. 앞서 시민단체 민생경제연구소와 서울의소리 등은 8월 26일 박 검사와 윤석열 전 대통령 등 관련자들을 무고와 직권남용 권리행사방해, 공무상 비밀누설, 정보통신망법상 명예훼손 등 혐의로 경찰청 국가수사본부에 고발했다.
https://www.yna.co.kr/view/akr2026111401.summary_zh: （首尔＝韩联社）记者郑智秀＝负责调查向朝鲜汇款事件的案件期间，前京畿道和平副州长李和英被指控诱导虚假证词、陷害李在明总统，仁川地方检察厅副厅长朴相勇此案已移送高位公职者犯罪调查处（公职者犯罪调查处）。警方14日称，首尔永登浦警察署于本月6日将朴检察官涉嫌妨害权利行使及滥用职权、陷害一案移送公职者犯罪调查处。此前，民间团体民生经济研究所和首尔之声音等机构已于8月26日，以涉嫌妨害权利行使、滥用职权、泄露公务秘密、违反《信息通信网法》诽谤等罪名，向警方国家调查本部控告朴检察官、尹锡悦前总统等有关人员。
https://www.yna.co.kr/view/akr2026111401.body: (서울=연합뉴스) 정지수 기자 = 쌍방울 대북송금 사건을 수사하며 이화영 전 경기도 평화부지사에게 허위 진술을 유도해 이재명 대통령을 무고했다는 의혹으로 고발된 박상용 인천지방공소청 부부장검사 사건이 고위공직자범죄수사처(공수처)로 이첩됐다. 14일 경찰에 따르면 서울 영등포경찰서는 박 검사의 무고·직권남용 권리행사방해 혐의 사건을 이달 6일 공수처로 이첩했다. 앞서 시민단체 민생경제연구소와 서울의소리 등은 8월 26일 박 검사와 윤석열 전 대통령 등 관련자들을 무고와 직권남용 권리행사방해, 공무상 비밀누설, 정보통신망법상 명예훼손 등 혐의로 경찰청 국가수사본부에 고발했다. 고발 내용은 당시 수원지방공소청에서 '쌍방울 대북송금 사건'을 수사하던 박상용 검사가 이 전 부지사 등을 회유했다는 이른바 '연어 술파티' 의혹과도 관련돼 있다. 고발인 측은 "박 검사가 구속 상태이던 이 전 부지사에게 '이재명 씨가 주범이 되고 이화영이 종범이 되는 식의 자백이 있어야 보석 등이 가능하다'는 취지로 말하며 허위진술을 유도했다"고 주장했다. 또 "박상용 검사가 중간에서 '죽겠다'고 말하는 등 윗선으로부터 상당한 압박을 받고 있다고 암시하고 있다"며 윤 전 대통령 등도 무고에 관여한 혐의가 있다고도 했다. 제보는 카카오톡 okjebo <저작권자(c) 연합뉴스, 무단 전재-재배포, AI 학습 및 활용 금지> 2026/11/14 08:31 송고 2026년11월14일 08시31분 송고

https://www.yna.co.kr/view/akr2026111401.body_zh: （首尔=韩联社）记者 정지수 = 涉嫌在调查“双鱼对朝汇款事件”过程中诱导前京畿道和平部长官李和荣作虚假陈述、诬陷总统李在明的仁川地方检察官厅副部长检察官朴相庸案，已移交高级公职者犯罪调查处（公职者犯罪调查处）。据警方14日消息，首尔永登浦警察局于本月6日将朴检察官涉嫌诬告、滥用职权妨碍权利行使一案移交公职者犯罪调查处。此前，民生经济研究所、首尔之声音等市民团体于8月26日以涉嫌诬告、滥用职权妨碍权利行使、泄露公务秘密、违反《信息通信网法》诽谤等罪名，向警察厅国家调查本部举报朴检察官、卸任总统尹锡悦等涉案人员。举报内容还涉及所谓“鳟鱼酒会”疑云，即在水原地方检察官厅调查“双鱼对朝汇款事件”期间，朴相庸检察官曾招揽前李部长官等人的说法。举报方主张：“朴检察官曾对处于被拘留状态的前李部长官说，必须作出‘李在明是主犯、李和荣是从犯’这样的自白，才能办理保释等事项，从而诱导其作出虚假陈述。”举报方又称：“朴相庸检察官在谈话中暗示自己从上级的到‘想杀了你’的说法中受到相当大的压力等。”并称卸任总统尹某等也涉嫌参与诬告。报道请通过KakaoTalk的okjebo获取。版权所有(c) 韩联社，禁止擅自转载、重新发布及用于人工智能学习和利用。2026/11/14 08:31发送，2026年11月14日08时31分发送

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/14/k.summary: John Shiklam in Kaduna Senator Sunday Katung, representing Kaduna South Senatorial District, has declared that the era of divisive politics in Kaduna State was over, saying what remains is politics of development and inclusion. A statement by spokesperson to Katung, Joseph Midat, in Kaduna yesterday, said the senator spoke on Thursday in Zaria at a town hall meeting with members of the Hausa Christian community and other stakeholders in Kaduna North Senatorial District.
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/14/k.summary_zh: 卡杜纳州参议员星期日·卡通代表卡杜纳南参议员选区宣布，卡杜纳州挑起族群分裂的政治时代已经结束，如今剩下的是促进发展和包容的政治。卡通发言人约瑟夫·米达特昨日在卡杜纳发表声明称，这位参议员于周四在扎里亚与豪萨族基督徒群体及卡杜纳北参议员选区的其他利益相关方举行了一场市民大会。
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/14/k.body: John Shiklam in Kaduna Senator Sunday Katung, representing Kaduna South Senatorial District, has declared that the era of divisive politics in Kaduna State was over, saying what remains is politics of development and inclusion. A statement by spokesperson to Katung, Joseph Midat, in Kaduna yesterday, said the senator spoke on Thursday in Zaria at a town hall meeting with members of the Hausa Christian community and other stakeholders in Kaduna North Senatorial District. Katung urged the community to support President Tinubu, Governor Uba Sani, and other All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates for the 2027 general elections. He said the administrations of Tinubu and Sani had demonstrated commitment to inclusive governance by ensuring that no community was left behind. Katung said, “Fairness, justice, and inclusion would remain the guiding principles of APC candidates, urging the youths to remain united, peaceful and politically active.” The senator described the numerical strength of the youths as a significant asset to the party’s electoral fortunes and pledged to continue to champion their cause. He also promised to work with other political leaders to attract development projects, appointments, and economic opportunities to their communities. “There is no division, no discrimination, and no going back. The era of politics of division is over, and what remains is politics of development, inclusion, and victory for all,” Katung said. He urged the Hausa Christian community to take ownership of the APC’s political project by mobilising support at polling units, wards, and local government areas to ensure victory for Tinubu, Sani and other APC candidates. He described the 2027 election as an opportunity for Kaduna State to demonstrate its commitment to unity, peace, progress, and continuity. Also, speaking at the event, Sani’s running for the 2027 election, Jerry Adams, commended Katung for organising the meeting and appreciated the stakeholders for their support. He highlighted interventions by the federal and state governments, including the establishment of federal institutions, skills acquisition centres across the three senatorial districts, a military cantonment, free compressed natural gas (CNG) buses and the recruitment and training of more than 1,000 Forest Guards. Adams also acknowledged federal appointments secured by Kaduna indigenes and urged the community to sustain its support for the APC ahead of the 2027 elections. Nigeria also recorded an increase in confirmed Lassa fever cases in epidemiological week 44 of 2026, with infections rising from nine in the previous week to 13, while four additional deaths were reported. The disease intervention centre had confirmed the Ebola infection on October 20, 2026 after the patient’s blood samples tested positive at the Abuja Reference Laboratory. After receiving preliminary treatment at an undisclosed private hospital in Abuja, she and her husband were subsequently medically evacuated to Switzerland via an air ambulance on October 26, 2026. Addressing journalists in his office in Abuja yesterday, NCDC Director General, Dr. Jide Idris, said the Swiss authorities have announced the recovery and discharge of the woman after testing negative He said index case tested negative after receiving treatment in an isolation facility in Switzerland. Meanwhile, the NCDC in its latest Lassa Fever Situation Report covering October 26 to November 1, disclosed that 179 suspected cases were recorded during the week, alongside 13 confirmed infections and four confirmed deaths. The new infections were reported in Ondo, Bauchi, Edo, Taraba and Nasarawa states, bringing the number of states affected by confirmed cases since the beginning of the year to 26. According to the report, the disease has spread across 122 local government areas (LGAs) nationwide, with a cumulative 8,968 suspected cases, 1,186 confirmed cases and 278 deaths recorded between epidemiological weeks one and 44. The cumulative Case Fatality Rate (CFR) currently stands at 23.4 per cent, compared with 18.3 per cent recorded during the corresponding period in 2025, when 177 deaths were reported from 966 confirmed cases. The NCDC noted that 87 per cent of all confirmed infections this year came from five states, namely Ondo, Bauchi, Taraba, Edo and Benue. Ondo accounted for the highest proportion of confirmed cases at 37 per cent, followed by Bauchi with 23 per cent, Taraba 12 per cent, Edo 10 per cent and Benue five per cent. The remaining 13 per cent were reported across 21 other states. The report identified people aged between 21 and 30 years as the most affected age group, although confirmed cases were recorded among individuals aged between one and 93 years. The median age was 31 years. It, however, noted that no new healthcare worker was infected during the reporting week. Despite fluctuations in weekly infections, the rising cumulative deaths and fatality rate have continued to raise concerns about early diagnosis, access to treatment and the country’s capacity to contain the disease. The NCDC identified late presentation of patients at health facilities as one of the major challenges contributing to the high fatality rate. Other challenges include the high cost of treatment, poor health-seeking behaviour, inadequate environmental sanitation, low public awareness and infections among healthcare workers. The agency also reported a shortage of laboratory reagents at the Irrua Specialist Teaching Hospital testing centre, a development that could affect timely diagnosis. In its response efforts, the NCDC said it had deployed national rapid response teams to seven high-burden states, strengthened surveillance and contact tracing, trained frontline healthcare workers and supported laboratory analysis to facilitate prompt diagnosis and treatment. It also disclosed that a 30-day healthcare worker protection plan had been developed to reduce infections among frontline medical personnel, while states were being encouraged to strengthen community engagement and prevention activities. The agency urged healthcare workers to maintain a high level of suspicion for Lassa fever, ensure timely referral and treatment of suspected cases, and adhere strictly to infection prevention and control procedures. It also called on Nigerians to maintain clean environments, store food in tightly covered containers, dispose of waste properly and eliminate conditions that encourage rodents to inhabit homes. Lassa fever is a viral disease primarily transmitted to humans through contact with food or household items contaminated by the urine or faeces of infected rats. The public was advised to seek medical attention promptly when experiencing symptoms such as fever, weakness and headache, particularly where there is a history of possible exposure. Unexplained bleeding is also a warning sign requiring urgent medical evaluation. The NCDC stressed that early detection, prompt treatment and collective responsibility remain critical to preventing further infections and deaths. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/14/k.title_zh: 卡图恩为蒂努布和萨尼争取豪萨基督徒支持，称卡杜纳州已经告别撕裂民心的政治
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/14/k.body_zh: 《THISDAY》记者John Shiklam报道：卡杜纳州参议员Sunday Katung代表卡杜纳南参议院选区宣布，卡杜纳州分裂政治的时代已经结束，剩下的是发展与包容的政治。Katung的发言人Joseph Midat昨日在卡杜纳发表声明称，这位参议员周四在扎里亚与豪萨族基督徒群体以及卡杜纳北参议院选区其他利益相关方举行了一次市政厅会议。Katung敦促该群体支持总统Tinubu、州长Uba Sani以及全尼日利亚进步大会党（APC）的其他2027年大选候选人。他说，Tinubu和Sani领导的政府通过确保不让任何群体掉队，展示了推行包容性治理的决心。Katung表示：“公平、正义与包容将继续作为APC候选人的指导原则，同时敦促年轻人保持团结、和平并积极参与政治。”这位参议员将年轻人的人数优势描述为该党选举前景的一项重要资产，并承诺继续为他们的事业奔走。他还承诺与其他政治领导人合作，为其所在群体争取发展项目、任命和经济机会。Katung说：“没有分裂，没有歧视，也不会倒退。分裂政治的时代已经结束，剩下的是发展、包容以及所有人共同胜利的政治。”他敦促豪萨族基督徒群体主动参与APC的政治事业，在投票站、选区和地方政府一级动员支持，确保Tinubu、Sani和其他APC候选人获胜。他表示，2027年选举是卡杜纳州展示其致力于团结、和平、进步与延续性的机会。也是Sani参加2027年竞选的竞选搭档Jerry Adams在活动上发言，赞扬Katung组织这次会议，并感谢利益相关方的支持。他强调，联邦和州政府采取了一系列干预措施，包括设立联邦机构、在三个参议院选区设立技能培训中心、兴建军事营区、提供免费压缩天然气（CNG）公交，以及招募并培训超过1,000名森林卫队。Adams还提到，为卡杜纳本地人争取到的联邦任命，并敦促该群体在2027年选举前继续支持APC。与此同时，尼日利亚还记录到2026年流行病学第44周拉沙热确诊病例上升，感染人数从前一周的9人增至13人，另报告4例新增死亡病例。疾病干预中心于2026年10月20日确认该埃博拉感染病例，因为患者的血样在阿布贾参考实验室检测呈阳性。她在阿布贾一家未公开名称的私立医院接受初步治疗后，于2026年10月26日随后与丈夫乘医疗救护机转送往瑞士。NCDC总干事Jide Idris博士昨日在阿布贾办公室接受记者采访时说，瑞士当局已宣布该女子康复出院，检测结果呈阴性。他说，指示病例在接受瑞士一处隔离设施的治疗后检测呈阴性。与此同时，NCDC在最新的《拉沙热疫情报告》中披露，该报告涵盖10月26日至11月1日，本周记录了179例疑似病例、13例确诊感染和4例确诊死亡。新增感染病例来自翁多州、包奇州、埃多州、塔拉巴州和纳萨拉瓦州，使年初以来报告确诊病例的州增至26个。报告显示，该疾病已蔓延至全国122个地方政府区（LGA），在流行病学第1至第44周期间累计记录8,968例疑似病例、1,186例确诊病例和278例死亡。目前累计病死率（CFR）为23.4%，高于2025年同期记录的18.3%；2025年同期共有966例确诊病例，报告177例死亡。NCDC指出，今年所有确诊感染病例中有87%来自5个州，即翁多州、包奇州、塔拉巴州、埃多州和贝努埃州。翁多州确诊病例占比最高，为37%；其次是包奇州，占23%；塔拉巴州占12%；埃多州占10%；贝努埃州占5%。其余13%分布在其他21个州。报告将21至30岁人群列为受影响最严重的年龄组，不过1至93岁人群均有确诊病例。中位年龄为31岁。不过，报告指出，本报告周内没有新的医护人员感染。尽管每周感染人数时有波动，但累计死亡人数和病死率持续上升，引发了人们对早期诊断、获得治疗以及该国控制疾病能力的担忧。NCDC称，患者到医疗机构就诊过晚，是导致高病死率的主要挑战之一。其他挑战还包括治疗费用高、就医行为不佳、环境卫生不足、公众意识低，以及医护人员感染。该机构还报告称，Irrua专科教学医院检测中心缺乏实验室试剂，这一情况可能影响及时诊断。在应对措施方面，NCDC表示已向7个高负担州派出国家级快速反应队，加强监测和接触者追踪，培训一线医护人员，并支持实验室分析，以促进及时诊断和治疗。该机构还透露，已制定一项为期30天的医护人员保护计划，以减少一线医务人员感染，同时鼓励各州加强社区参与和预防活动。NCDC敦促医护人员对拉沙热保持高度警觉，确保疑似病例得到及时转诊和治疗，并严格遵守感染预防与控制规程。它还呼吁尼日利亚人保持环境清洁，将食物储存在密闭容器中妥善处理废物，并消除有利于啮齿动物在住宅中栖息的环境。拉沙热是一种病毒性疾病，主要通过接触被受感染老鼠的尿液或粪便污染的食物或家居用品传播给人类。公众如出现发热、虚弱和头痛等症状，尤其是有可能接触史时，应尽快就医。无法解释的出血也是需要紧急医疗评估的危险信号。NCDC强调，早期发现、及时治疗和共同责任对于防止进一步感染和死亡仍然至关重要。THISDAY于1995年1月22日创办，由THISDAY AFP 통신 등 외신에 따르면 올리비아 웨일스 백악관 공보 담당은 이날 기자들에게 미중러 정상이 17∼19일 중국 선전에서 열리는 아시아태평양경제협력체(APEC) 정상회의를 계기로 19일 3자 회동을 한다고 밝혔다. 웨일스는 "트럼프 대통령은 다른 의제들과 더불어 전 세계 핵무기 감축 문제를 논의하겠다는 입장을 분명히 해왔다"며 "트럼프 대통령은 이러한 핵확산이 매우 위험하다고 보고 있다"고 설명했다. 미 정부 고위 당국자들에 따르면 트럼프 대통령은 이번 3자 회담에서 핵 감축과 함께 현재 진행 중인 대(對)이란 전쟁 문제를 의제로 올릴 예정이다. 다만, 우크라이나 전쟁은 논의하지 않을 전망이다. 익명을 요구한 미 고위 당국자는 "대통령은 시 주석, 푸틴 대통령과의 3자 회담에서 이란 문제를 논의할 의향이 있다"면서도 우크라이나 전쟁에 대해서는 미국이 러시아, 우크라이나와 함께 가동 중인 '완전히 별개의 협상 트랙'이 있다고 선을 그었다. 트럼프 대통령의 특사들은 최근 아랍에미리트(UAE) 아부다비에서 러시아, 우크라이나 측과 3자 비공개 협상을 벌였다. 미 고위 당국자는 "중국은 그 협상 트랙의 일원이 아니기 때문에 그 자리에서 우크라이나 문제를 논의하는 것은 적절하지 않다"고 말했다. 또한 한 미국 당국자는 트럼프 대통령이 다음 주 아시아 방문 기간 김정은 북한 국무위원장과 만나지 않을 예정이라고 말했다고 로이터 통신이 보도했다. 트럼프 대통령이 15∼17일 필리핀 마닐라에서 열리는 동남아시아국가연합(ASEAN) 정상회의나 17∼19일 중국 선전에서 열리는 APEC 정상회의에서 어떤 방식으로든 김 위원장과 만날 계획이 현재로서는 없다는 입장을 밝힌 것이다. 제보는 카카오톡 okjebo <저작권자(c) 연합뉴스, 무단 전재-재배포, AI 학습 및 활용 금지> 2026/11/14 11:07 송고 2026년11월14일 11시07분 송고 지난 2019년 6월 도널드 트럼프 미국 대통령(왼쪽)과 김정은 북한 국무위원장이 판문점 군사분계선 북측 지역에서 만나 인사한 뒤 남측 지역으로 향하고 있다. https://www.yna.co.kr/view/akr2026111402.body_zh: （首尔=韩联社）记者金升旭报道称，白宫宫长办公室于13日（当地时间）宣布，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普、中国国家主席习近平以及俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京将于19日在中国深圳举行史上首次美中俄三国领导人会晤。据法新社等外媒报道，白宫新闻秘书办公室负责新闻发布事务的奥利维亚·韦尔斯当天对记者表示，美中俄三国领导人将以17日至19日在中国深圳举行的亚太经合组织（APEC）领导人会议为契机，于19日举行三方会晤。韦尔斯说：“特朗普总统已明确表示，除其他议程外，还将讨论全球核武器削减问题”，并称“特朗普总统认为，这种核扩散极其危险”。据美国政府高级官员透露，特朗普总统计划在此次三方会谈中，除核军备削减外，还将把目前进行中的对伊朗战争问题列为议题。不过，预计不会讨论乌克兰战争。一名要求匿名的美国高级官员表示：“总统有意在与习近平主席、普京总统的三方会谈中讨论伊朗问题”，同时强调，对于乌克兰战争，美国与俄罗斯、乌克兰正在开展的是“一条完全不同的谈判轨道”。特朗普总统的特使近期在阿拉伯联合酋长国（UAE）阿布扎比与俄罗斯和乌克兰方面举行了三方闭门谈判。一名美国高级官员说：“由于中国不是该谈判轨道的成员，因此在那个场合讨论乌克兰问题并不合适”。此外，据路透社报道，一名美国官员表示，特朗普总统预计在下周访问亚洲期间不会会见朝鲜国务委员会委员金正恩。特朗普总统明确表示，目前无论如何都没有计划在15日至17日在菲律宾马尼拉举行的东南亚国家联盟（ASEAN）领导人会议，以及17日至19日在中国深圳举行的APEC领导人会议上，以任何方式与金正恩委员长会面。投稿邮箱：KakaoTalk okjebo。版权所有© 韩联社，禁止擅自转载、发行及用于人工智能学习和应用。2026年11月14日11时07分发布。2019年6月，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普（左）与朝鲜国务委员会委员金正恩在板门店军事分界线北侧地区会面并致意后，前往南侧地区。[摄影：裴载民]

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/14/2.summary_zh: 在2027年大选前夕，逾3,000名女性领袖、决策者、外交官和公民社会人士昨日齐聚阿布贾，参加首届“尼日利亚女性争取和平与民主峰会及2026年颁奖礼”。本次峰会以“女性成为和平、民主和包容性治理的推动者”为主题，在博拉·艾哈迈德·蒂努布国际会议中心举行，由全国妇女协会理事会（NCWS）主办，该组织全国主席为Edna D.D.。
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/14/2.body: Ahead of the 2027 general elections, over 3,000 women leaders, policymakers, diplomats and civil society actors converged on Abuja yesterday for the maiden edition of the Nigeria Women for Peace and Democracy Summit and Awards 2026. The summit themed, ‘Women as Catalysts for Peace, Democracy and Inclusive Governance’, held at the Bola Ahmed Tinubu International Conference Centre, was hosted by the National Council of Women’s Societies (NCWS) under the leadership of its National President, Edna D.D. Azura. In her welcome remarks, Azura said the summit was deliberately convened ahead of the 2027 general elections to position women not as spectators in democracy, but as drivers of peace, governance and national stability. “Nigerian women must be recognised as key actors in peace, democracy, national unity and sustainable development. We are not just beneficiaries of democracy, we are its builders,” she said. She explained that the gathering would provide a platform for dialogue on democracy, governance, women’s leadership, peace-building and conflict prevention, bringing together delegates from across Nigeria’s political, ethnic, religious and generational divides, drawn from government institutions, security agencies, traditional and religious institutions, the private sector, diplomatic missions, development organisations and civil society groups. Addressing the summit, the Minister of Women Affairs and Social Development, Imaan Sulaiman-Ibrahim, stressed that sustainable peace and national security cannot be achieved without the full inclusion of women in decision-making. She said the federal government under President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda, is implementing transformative policies and programmes to strengthen women’s leadership, expand protection for survivors of gender-based violence, and promote women’s participation in peace, security and governance. “Women are not just victims of conflict, they are catalysts for peace. When you empower a woman, you secure a family, you stabilise a community, and you strengthen a nation,” the minister said. She noted that the ministry is anchoring its interventions on key national and international frameworks, including the National Gender Policy, the Violence Against Persons (Prohibition) Act, the Child Rights Act, the Women’s Economic Empowerment Policy, and Nigeria’s Third National Action Plan on Women, Peace and Security. A major highlight of the summit was the Nigeria Women for Peace and Democracy Awards, which honoured outstanding individuals, institutions, development partners, humanitarian organisations and women leaders whose contributions have advanced peacebuilding, democratic governance, women’s empowerment and nation-building. Organisers said the awards were instituted to celebrate women who are often overlooked despite their sacrifice and service in communities across the country. The NCWS is Nigeria’s oldest and largest national women’s organisation, with international affiliation to the International Council of Women (ICW) since 1958, a global umbrella body founded in 1888 and committed to promoting women’s rights, education, economic empowerment, health, welfare, peace and leadership. With Friday’s summit, stakeholders say the NCWS has once again reaffirmed its role as the foremost voice for Nigerian women, pushing for inclusion, not as a favour, but as a necessity for a peaceful and democratic Nigeria. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/14/2.title_zh: 2027年选举：女性引领争取和平与民主的倡议 summit
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/14/2.body_zh: 在2027年大选前夕，3000多名女性领导人、政策制定者、外交官和民间社会人士昨日齐聚阿布贾，参加首届“2026年尼日利亚妇女、和平与民主峰会暨颁奖礼”。本次峰会以“女性成为和平、民主和包容性治理的推动者”为主题，在博拉·艾哈迈德·蒂努布国际会议中心举行，由全国妇女组织理事会（NCWS）主办，理事会全国主席埃德娜·D.D.阿祖拉担任领导工作。阿祖拉在欢迎辞中说，峰会有意安排在2027年大选前夕举行，旨在让女性成为和平、治理和国家稳定的推动者，而非民主进程的旁观者。她说：“尼日利亚妇女必须被视为和平、民主、国家统一和可持续发展的关键行动者。我们不仅是民主的受益者，更是民主的建设者。”她表示，此次聚会将为围绕民主、治理、女性领导力、和平建设和冲突预防展开对话提供平台，汇聚来自尼日利亚不同政治、族群、宗教和世代群体的代表，他们来自政府机构、安全部门、传统和宗教机构、私营部门、外交使团、发展组织及民间社会团体。妇女事务和社会发展部长伊曼·苏莱曼-易卜拉欣在峰会上强调，如果不能让女性充分参与决策，就无法实现可持续和平与国家安全。她说，博拉·艾哈迈德·蒂努布总统领导的联邦政府正在“更新希望议程”框架下实施变革性政策和方案，以加强女性领导力、扩大对性别暴力幸存者的保护，并推动女性参与和平、安全和治理事务。部长说：“女性不仅是冲突的受害者，也是和平的推动者。赋予一名女性力量，就意味着保障一个家庭、稳定一个社区并强化一个国家。”她指出，该部正在以多项关键国家和国际框架为依据开展干预措施，包括《国家性别政策》《反侵害人法》《儿童权利法》《妇女经济赋权政策》以及尼日利亚《妇女、和平与安全第三次国家行动计划》。本次峰会的一大亮点是“尼日利亚妇女、和平与民主奖”，表彰了在推动和平建设、民主治理、妇女赋权和国家建设方面作出突出贡献的个人、机构、发展伙伴、人道主义组织和女性领导人。组织方表示，设立这些奖项旨在表彰那些为全国各地社区作出牺牲和贡献，却常常未获关注的女性。全国妇女组织理事会（NCWS）是尼日利亚历史最悠久、规模最大的全国性妇女组织，自1958年起加入国际妇女理事会（ICW）。该机构是一个全球性联合组织，成立于1888年，致力于促进妇女权利、教育、经济赋权、健康、福利、和平与领导力。相关利益人士表示，通过周五举行的此次峰会，NCWS再次确认了其作为尼日利亚妇女最重要代言机构的角色，持续推动女性全面参与——这并非一种优待，而是实现和平与民主的尼日利亚的必要条件。THISDAY于1995年1月22日创刊，由THISDAY NEWSPAPERS LTD.出版，地址为尼日利亚拉各斯阿帕帕溪路35号，在尼日利亚36个州、联邦首都辖区以及世界各地设有办事处。该报是尼日利亚最具权威性的新闻媒体，通过各类平台覆盖政治、商业、专业和外交精英群体及更广泛的中产阶层，同时充当有抱负者和千禧一代的新思想、文化与技术交汇点。这份报纸是一项公共信任事业，以追求真理与理性为宗旨，报道范围涵盖突发新闻、政治、商业、金融市场、艺术、体育和社区议题，直至人与社会的交汇点。您可以发送电子邮件至：hello@thisdaylive.com，或访问我们的联系我们页面

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/14/c.title: China’s ICE Vehicle Push to Africa: What It Means for Nigeria
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/14/c.summary: China’s continued shipment of large numbers of internal combustion-engine (ICE) vehicles to Nigeria and other African markets is being driven less by a retreat from electric mobility than by a major restructuring of the Chinese automobile industry, with manufacturers increasingly looking overseas for markets, revenue and capacity utilisation.
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/14/c.summary_zh: 中国继续向尼日利亚及其他非洲市场大量运输内燃机（ICE）汽车，其主要驱动力并非从电动出行领域退却，而是中国汽车行业正在进行重大重组；制造商越来越积极地到海外寻找市场、收入和产能利用空间。
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/14/c.body: China’s continued shipment of large numbers of internal combustion-engine (ICE) vehicles to Nigeria and other African markets is being driven less by a retreat from electric mobility than by a major restructuring of the Chinese automobile industry, with manufacturers increasingly looking overseas for markets, revenue and capacity utilisation. The development has important implications for Nigeria, where weak charging infrastructure, unreliable electricity supply, high vehicle acquisition costs and limited consumer purchasing power continue to constrain the mass adoption of electric vehicles (EVs). China has become the world’s dominant vehicle manufacturing base while simultaneously undergoing one of the fastest transitions from petrol and diesel vehicles to new-energy vehicles. The result is a growing pool of conventional vehicles that manufacturers can still sell profitably in markets where the transition to electric mobility is slower. The International Energy Agency (IEA) said Chinese vehicle exports increased sharply in the first half of 2026 as domestic sales weakened, with total Chinese car exports rising 65 per cent year-on-year. Although electric-car exports grew even faster, ICE vehicles remain a major component of China’s overseas shipments. For Africa, the continent’s relatively young motorisation market makes it particularly attractive, according to IEA. Unlike Europe and some Asian markets, where stringent emissions regulations and EV incentives are accelerating the replacement of petrol and diesel vehicles, many African countries still depend heavily on conventional vehicles, particularly imported used cars. Nigeria is a major example. The country’s vehicle market remains overwhelmingly dependent on petrol and diesel technology, while the infrastructure required for large-scale EV adoption is still developing. China’s strategy therefore allows its automakers to serve different markets according to their level of technological transition. EVs can be targeted at markets with adequate charging networks and supportive policies, while ICE vehicles can continue flowing into markets where consumers prioritise affordability, driving range, easy access to mechanics and the availability of fuel. There is also a broader industrial dimension. China’s highly competitive automobile industry has experienced intense price competition and excess production capacity. Overseas markets provide manufacturers with an outlet for vehicles that may face declining demand at home. The IEA noted that Chinese automakers are increasingly relying on overseas markets as domestic growth slows, with major manufacturers setting ambitious export targets. For Nigeria, the influx presents both opportunities and risks. On the positive side, increased Chinese competition could make vehicles more affordable, expand consumer choice and force established global brands to reduce prices. It could also create opportunities for local assembly, component manufacturing, servicing and technical employment if Nigeria successfully links vehicle imports to an industrialisation strategy. But continued dependence on ICE imports could also slow Nigeria’s own transition to cleaner transportation. Nigeria’s Energy Transition Plan envisages a gradual shift towards electric mobility, while the country’s automotive policy seeks greater local vehicle production and increased EV manufacturing. The Nigerian Automotive Industry Development Plan, for instance, targets 30 per cent of locally produced vehicles being electric by 2032. The danger, therefore, is that Nigeria could become a dumping ground for ageing or declining ICE technology just as major manufacturers are moving their technological investments towards batteries, software and electric drivetrains. There is also an environmental and economic cost. Continued dependence on petrol and diesel vehicles means higher exposure to fuel-price shocks, import dependence and transport-sector emissions. Yet the answer is not necessarily to shut the door on Chinese ICE vehicles immediately. Nigeria’s transition must reflect its infrastructure realities. The government would need to expand charging infrastructure, stabilise electricity supply, establish battery and vehicle standards, develop local technical capacity and create incentives for manufacturers to assemble EVs locally. Importantly, 2035 is not a blanket deadline for China to stop producing or exporting every ICE vehicle. China’s official New Energy Vehicle Industry Development Plan says that by 2035, electric vehicles are expected to become the mainstream of new vehicle sales, while public transportation is expected to be fully electrified. A 2025 Chinese transport-energy guideline similarly states that by 2035, pure electric vehicles should become the mainstream of new vehicle sales. China’s target is market dominance by new-energy vehicles, not an announced universal ban on ICE vehicles by 2035. Conventional vehicles can therefore continue to be manufactured, sold or exported, particularly to markets such as Africa where demand remains strong. For Nigeria, this creates a policy dilemma: Chinese ICE vehicles may provide immediate, relatively affordable mobility, but an uncontrolled influx could lock the country into yesterday’s automotive technology just as the world’s largest vehicle manufacturing power accelerates towards tomorrow’s. He explained: “Let me be clear, we are not anti-China. We are pro-Nigeria. “We welcome Chery, Jetour, GAC, Changan, Geely, BYD. Their arrival has forced prices down. A Nigerian can now buy a brand new SUV for N28m instead of N55m. That is good for the consumer. Competition is good. But what we are seeing today is not competition. It is dumping. These are not assembled in Nigeria. Over 95% are imported fully built. Meanwhile, our own assemblers – Innoson in Nnewi, PAN in Kaduna, Nord in Lagos, Stallion in Lagos – are operating at less than 20% capacity. China is moving to EVs at home and pushing its excess ICE production to Africa. Nigeria is becoming the dumping ground. He said, “That is not a level playing field. That is policy failure. If you want to sell more than 1,000 cars a year in Nigeria, you must assemble in Nigeria within 3 years. If you sell cars in Nigeria, you must guarantee parts for 10 years and train Nigerian technicians. Nigeria should not replace tokunbo dependence with Chinese dependence. He stated that, “The biggest enemy of our sector is not China. It is our own policy inconsistency. “The National Automotive Industry Development Plan (NAIDP) says 35% for fully built, 10% for SKD, 5% for CKD. In practice, waivers are given to a few importers to bring fully built cars at 20%. That single waiver kills 10 assemblers.” a) Zero Waivers for Fully Built Cars. Publish all waivers. No secret waivers. b) 10-Year Policy Lock. No investor will build a $50m assembly plant if policy can change in 6 months. Lock it. Local Parts Manufacturing. Nigeria imports $180m in parts from China, $61m from Japan. We must give Pioneer Status to local brake pad, filter, battery and tyre manufacturers. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/14/c.title_zh: 中国向非洲推广纯电动汽车：对尼日利亚意味着什么
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/14/c.body_zh: 中国继续向尼日利亚及其他非洲市场大量运送内燃机（ICE）汽车，其驱动力并非中国放弃电动出行，而是中国汽车产业正在进行重大重组。制造商日益转向海外市场，以寻找销路、收入并提高产能利用率。这一趋势对尼日利亚具有重要影响，因为充电基础设施薄弱、电力供应不稳定、购车成本高昂以及消费者购买力有限，仍在制约电动汽车（EV）的普及。中国已成为全球主导的汽车制造基地，同时也在经历从汽油和柴油汽车向新能源汽车过渡的最快阶段之一。这一结果意味着，传统汽车的数量不断增加；在向电动出行转型较慢的市场，制造商仍能以盈利方式销售这些汽车。国际能源署（IEA）表示，2026年上半年，随着国内销售走弱，中国汽车出口大幅增长，中国汽车出口总量同比增长65%。尽管电动汽车出口增长得更快，但ICE汽车仍是中国海外出口的重要组成部分。IEA称，非洲相对年轻的汽车化市场尤其具有吸引力。与欧洲和部分亚洲市场不同，那里严格的排放法规和EV激励措施正在加速汽油和柴油汽车被替代，而许多非洲国家仍高度依赖传统汽车，尤其是进口二手车。尼日利亚就是一个典型例子。该国的汽车市场仍压倒性地依赖汽油和柴油技术，而大规模采用EV所需的基础设施仍在发展之中。因此，中国的战略使其汽车制造商能够根据不同市场的技术转型程度开展业务。EV可以瞄准充电网络完善且政策支持的市场，而ICE汽车则可以继续流入消费者重视价格可负担性、续航里程、便于维修以及燃油供应的市场。这背后还有更广泛的产业层面。中国竞争激烈的汽车行业经历了激烈的价格竞争，并面临产能过剩。海外市场为制造商提供了出口渠道，以消化那些在国内可能面临需求下降的汽车。IEA指出，随着国内增长放缓，中国汽车制造商越来越依赖海外市场，主要制造商还设定了雄心勃勃的出口目标。对尼日利亚而言，大量涌入既带来机遇，也带来风险。从积极一面看，中国企业加大竞争可能使汽车价格更加亲民，扩大消费者选择，并迫使成熟的全球品牌降价。如果尼日利亚成功将汽车进口与工业化战略相结合，竞争还可能为本地组装、零部件制造、维修服务和技术就业创造机会。但持续依赖进口ICE汽车，也可能拖慢尼日利亚自身向更清洁交通方式转型的进程。尼日利亚《能源转型计划》设想逐步转向电动出行，该国的汽车政策则寻求提高本地汽车产量并增加EV制造。例如，《尼日利亚汽车产业发展计划》提出，到2032年，本地生产汽车中30%应为电动汽车。因此，危险在于，正当主要制造商将技术投资转向电池、软件和电驱动系统之际，尼日利亚可能成为老旧或落后ICE技术的倾销地。这还会带来环境和经济代价。持续依赖汽油和柴油汽车意味着更容易受到燃油价格冲击，对进口依赖加深，并增加交通运输业排放。然而，解决办法未必是立即将中国ICE汽车拒之门外。尼日利亚的转型必须反映其基础设施现实。政府需要扩大充电基础设施、稳定电力供应、建立电池和汽车标准、发展本地技术能力，并为制造商在本地组装EV提供激励。重要的是，2035年并不意味着中国必须全面停止生产和出口所有ICE汽车。中国官方的《新能源汽车产业发展规划》提出，到2035年，电动汽车预计将成为新车销售的主流，公共交通预计将全面实现电动化。2025年中国交通能源指导文件同样指出，到2035年，纯电动汽车应成为新车销售的主流。中国的目标是让新能源汽车占据市场主导地位，而不是宣布到2035年对ICE汽车实施全面禁令。因此，传统汽车仍可继续生产、销售或出口，尤其是在非洲等需求依然强劲的市场。对尼日利亚而言，这造成了一项政策困境：中国ICE汽车可以立即提供相对廉价的出行方式，但若不加控制地大量涌入，就可能在全球最大汽车制造国加速迈向未来技术之际，把这个国家锁定在昨天的汽车技术上。他解释道：“我要明确说明，我们不反对中国，我们支持尼日利亚。“我们欢迎奇瑞、捷途、广汽、长安、吉利、比亚迪。他们的到来迫使价格下降。尼日利亚人现在可以花2800万奈拉买到一辆全新SUV，而不必花5500万奈拉。这对消费者有利。竞争是好事。但我们今天看到的不是竞争，而是倾销。这些车不是在尼日利亚组装的。超过95%都是以整车形式进口的。与此同时，我们自己的组装厂——位于恩韦的Innoson、位于卡杜纳的PAN、位于拉各斯的Nord和Stallion——产能利用率均不足20%。中国在国内转向EV，同时把过剩的ICE产能推向非洲。尼日利亚正在成为倾销地。他说：“这不是公平的竞争环境。这是政策失灵。如果你想在尼日利亚每年销售超过1000辆汽车，就必须在3年内于尼日利亚组装。如果你在尼日利亚销售汽车，就必须保证10年的零部件供应，并培训尼日利亚技术员。尼日利亚不应在摆脱对‘tokunbo’的依赖之后，又转而依赖中国。他表示：“我们这个行业最大的敌人不是中国，而是我们自身政策的不一致。“《国家汽车产业发展计划》（NAIDP）规定，整车进口税率为35%，SKD为10%，CKD为5%。但在实际操作中，少数进口商获得了20%的整车进口豁免。仅这一项豁免就足以让10家组装厂无以为继。a）对整车实行零豁免。公布所有豁免情况，不允许任何秘密豁免。b）锁定10年政策。如果政策6个月就能改变，没有投资者会建设一座价值5000万美元的组装厂。因此必须锁定政策。本地零部件制造。尼日利亚每年从中国进口1.8亿美元零部件，从日本进口6100万美元零部件。我们必须给予本地制动片、滤清器、电池和轮胎制造商‘先锋地位’。我们还必须执行SON标准——我们市场上60%的零部件都是假货。”THISDAY于1995年1月22日创办，由THISDAY
